name: Siphon
description: Bring Stremio catalogs, metadata, subtitles and stream versions to native Jellyfin libraries.

versions.changelog: Identify failed catalog subscriptions in Tasks and synchronization history with stable identities and safe causes, persisted across restarts without exposing credentials or upstream errors. Partial synchronization still reports Failed and preserves prior media. Fix equivalent GUID handling and keep non-playable metadata available for canonical and retired versions so native progress/stop reports can save resume state without reopening retired sources or crossing user boundaries. Adds English/French failure details and regression coverage for catalog preservation, safe persistence and playback reporting.

Fix a Jellyfin startup regression when an existing Siphon catalog exceeds 256 MiB. Large valid state files load and save without truncation, preserving native identities, ownership and metadata; the 100,000-item limit and atomic writes remain enforced. Prevent calendar notification starvation under brief publication-lock contention and create generated native collections with their initial members, preserving manual additions. Correct native login and notification smoke synchronization, allow matching source/catalog versions after publication, update the Node.js action runtime, and pin Linux CI to Ubuntu 24.04. Detailed release notes now come from annotated tags rather than a tracked notes file.

Siphon 1.5.0.0: private user addon profiles, native collections and saved additions, selected-version HTTP/P2P downloads, source and metadata diagnostics, selective history recovery, followed-series calendar and opt-in notifications, targeted synchronization, provider quotas and shared caching, IntroDB timings, and bounded opt-in P2P playback. Includes media-response validation and the unchanged supplied icon. Persistent offline queues, offline HLS exports and external webhooks remain unreleased 1.6 features.
